title: Sanitized adaptation of IAB's own 2.6 section 6 video request and inline VAST response examples

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 section 6.2.4 Example 4 - Video (request) and section 6.3.2 Example 2 - VAST XML Document Returned Inline (response)
source.license: CC BY 3.0 (IAB OpenRTB 2.6 example request/response text); MIT (sanitization edits, host/domain rewrites and fixture identifiers)
source.notes: Response example cited from the same document, anchor #vastxml (section 6.3.2). All source records are retained in assets/sources.json by reference.sourceIds.

modifications: buyeruid removed entirely; the example's real-looking long numeric user.id replaced with a short fixture id; user.data profiling segments removed.

site.domain/page/ref and device.ua rewritten to *.example.test hosts and a synthetic user agent string; no real company, tracker or referrer domain retained. device.ip (absent from the original example) added as the documentation-only address 198.51.100.14 so the pair carries no device.ip/ua deviation.

Response bid.impid corrected from the example's unrelated '2' to '1' so it resolves against this request's imp.id (the two examples are drawn from different subsections of the same document and were never a matched pair on the wire). nurl and the VAST AdSystem/Impression/ClickThrough/MediaFile URLs rewritten to *.example.test; AdSystem text 'SpotXchange' replaced with the fixture label 'ortbtools test fixture'.

adomain added to the response bid (absent in the original response example) so crosscheck has a declared advertiser domain to inspect; bid.id and bid.crid are new synthetic identifiers, also absent from the original response example.

The legacy 'apis' field name from the original request example (OpenRTB's Video object field is 'api', not 'apis') was dropped rather than corrected, to avoid asserting behavior for a field this pair does not intend to test. imp.video.mimes drops the example's third entry 'application/javascript' (a companion-API MIME, not itself validated by imp.video.mimes) since this pair does not intend to test it either.

AdTitle content changed from the example's CDATA 'Sample VAST' to this case's id, matching the marker convention used by every other case in this format; companionad[0].expdir and companionad[1].battr (both present in the original request example) were dropped as not exercised by this pair; the response Impression element gained a CDATA wrapper the original example did not use, consistent with the CDATA style used elsewhere in this fixture's VAST.
provenance.sanitized: No production payload or PII used. buyeruid and the real-looking numeric user id are removed; all resource and tracking hosts end in .test; external network must remain blocked.

pairApplicability.note: Request and response are drawn from different subsections of the same IAB document; impid was corrected to pair them (see modifications).

specNotes: SeatBid.seat is intentionally omitted, matching the original IAB example — it is optional (OpenRTB 2.6 Object: SeatBid) and this pair checks that its absence produces no finding.

MediaFile bitrate=256 sits below imp.video.minbitrate=300, unmodified from the original example; no rule in packages/core cross-validates MediaFile bitrate against minbitrate/maxbitrate today, so this is an unverified boundary, not an asserted defect.
bid.price 3.00 against bidfloor 0.03 (both figures unmodified from the two source examples).
Validity describes protocol structure and declared constraints; generated media bytes must be checked against declared MIME/duration before playback tests.
Current Inspector contract displays VAST as inert XML; text visibility must not be counted as creative rendering or media playback.
fixtureAssets lists controlled resources; intercept .test URLs locally. Never fetch public advertising/tracking hosts.
notes: Core observations in the source archive were deliberately excluded from expectations. Protocol metadata may describe a vendor-specific 2.x carrier; it does not claim a normative minor-version inference.

preview.capabilityGap: The current VAST preview is inert XML; video/audio playback and Wrapper resolution are not implemented.
